title: ICU management by specialist – first day
criteria: Management of a patient in an ICU by a specialist or consultant physician on the first day of the ICU admission. It is a global daily fee that covers all ICU attendances (including by support medical staff), ECG monitoring, arterial sampling and bladder catheterisation on that day.
rules: Must be provided by a specialist/consultant physician who is immediately available and exclusively rostered for intensive care (TN.1.11)

'Immediately available' = predominantly present in the ICU during normal hours (absences up to about 2 h allowed if cover is in place); after hours, immediately contactable and able to return within a reasonable time. 'Exclusively rostered' = sole clinical commitment is intensive care (TN.1.9)

Unit must meet the MBS ICU definition: can ventilate >24 h and do invasive cardiovascular monitoring; intensivist exclusively rostered in normal hours; doctor in hospital and immediately available 24/7; RN at least 18 h/day; defined admission/discharge policies (TN.1.9)
Once per calendar day per patient, however many intensivists are involved; itemise by calendar day, not 24-h period (TN.1.9, TN.1.11)
Do not bill for very short stays (about <2 h) with minimal ICU management (TN.1.11)
Post-operative ICU admission is payable only where there is clear clinical justification for intensive care (TN.1.9)
Not claimable with 13899 on the same day (TN.1.11)
13839 (arterial puncture) is not payable in addition on the same day (TN.1.10)
ECG monitoring, arterial sampling and bladder catheterisation are included – do not bill them separately
Other specialists asked to attend (not managing the ICU care) can claim their own attendance items; endorse their account to show the consultation was not part of ICU management (TN.1.9)
Patient moved between ICUs: the two units sort out billing between themselves (TN.1.11)
schedule_date: MBS Online, schedule fees updated 1 July 2026 (pages read 7 Nov 2026)

title: ICU management by specialist – each subsequent day
criteria: Management of a patient in an ICU by a specialist or consultant physician on each day after the first. It is a global daily fee that covers all ICU attendances, ECG monitoring, arterial sampling and bladder catheterisation on that day.
rules: Must be provided by a specialist who is immediately available and exclusively rostered for intensive care (TN.1.11; definitions in TN.1.9)
Once per calendar day per patient, however many intensivists are involved; itemise by calendar day (TN.1.9, TN.1.11)
Not claimable with 13899 on the same day (TN.1.11)
13839 is not payable in addition on the same day (TN.1.10)
Do not bill for very short stays (about <2 h) with minimal ICU management (TN.1.11)
Unit must meet the TN.1.9 ICU definition; for NICU, the baby must meet the TN.1.9 admission criteria
Non-managing specialists asked to attend can claim separately, with the account endorsed (TN.1.9)

title: Airway access + start of ventilation in ICU
criteria: Establishing airway access and starting mechanical ventilation in an ICU, by a specialist or consultant physician, so the patient can go on to ongoing ventilatory support. It must not be associated with any anaesthetic service. It covers only establishing the airway and starting ventilation; ongoing ventilator management is 13882.
rules: FORM LABEL NOTE: the MBS wording does not say 'day 1' and does not include ventilation management – it covers the intubation/initiation event in ICU
Not payable if associated with any anaesthetic service (descriptor)
Patient must be in an ICU that meets the TN.1.9 definition; TN.1.9's once-per-day rule for ICU management items applies
The item page states no other frequency limit or co-claiming exclusion
Intubation outside the ICU for later ICU ventilation is 13857

title: Ventilatory support management in ICU – each day
criteria: Daily management of ventilatory support in an ICU by a specialist or consultant physician who is immediately available and exclusively rostered for intensive care. Covers invasive ventilation, and covers NIV only where the only alternative to NIV would be invasive ventilation.
rules: Descriptor says 'each day'. FORM LABEL NOTE: 'subsequent' is not in the MBS wording, so day 1 appears claimable too (e.g. alongside 13881) – this reading of the descriptor is an interpretation
NIV qualifies only where invasive ventilation would be the only alternative
Requires an immediately available, exclusively rostered ICU specialist (descriptor, TN.1.11)
Once per day per patient, however many intensivists are involved (TN.1.9)
NICU: baby must meet the TN.1.9 admission criteria

title: Continuous pressure monitoring in ICU (per pressure type)
criteria: Continuous monitoring through an indwelling catheter in an ICU of central venous, pulmonary arterial, systemic arterial or cardiac intracavity pressure. Must be managed by a specialist/consultant physician who is immediately available and exclusively rostered for intensive care. Claimed once for each type of pressure per calendar day, up to 4 pressures.
rules: Once per pressure type per calendar day, maximum 4 pressures per patient per day, however many practitioners are involved (descriptor, TN.1.11)
The four MBS pressure types are CVP, pulmonary arterial pressure, systemic arterial pressure and cardiac intracavity pressure
Must be in an ICU that meets TN.1.9, with an exclusively rostered ICU specialist
Pressure monitoring outside the ICU by practitioners not associated with the ICU is item 11600, not 13876 (TN.1.11)
The MBS has no letter suffixes. A/C/P/R on the form are the practice's own shorthand; on the Medicare claim, each pressure is a separate line of item 13876

Billing more than one 13876 line on the same day will usually need Medicare's 'not duplicate service' override plus a note naming the pressure. This is general Medicare claiming practice, not an MBS note – confirm with the claiming software

title: 13876 – systemic arterial pressure (practice code A)
criteria: Practice shorthand for item 13876 claimed for continuous monitoring of systemic arterial pressure through an indwelling arterial line in ICU. 'A' is not an MBS suffix; claim it as 13876. All 13876 criteria apply.
rules: Counts as 1 of the maximum 4 pressure types per calendar day
Requires an exclusively rostered ICU specialist and an ICU that meets TN.1.9
Arterial line insertion is a separate item (13842)

title: 13876 – central venous pressure (practice code C)
criteria: Practice shorthand for item 13876 claimed for continuous CVP monitoring through an indwelling central venous catheter in ICU. 'C' is not an MBS suffix; claim it as 13876. All 13876 criteria apply.
rules: Counts as 1 of the maximum 4 pressure types per calendar day
Requires an exclusively rostered ICU specialist and an ICU that meets TN.1.9
CVC insertion is a separate item (13815)

title: 13876 – pulmonary arterial pressure (practice code P)
criteria: Practice shorthand for item 13876 claimed for continuous pulmonary arterial pressure monitoring through a PA catheter in ICU. 'P' is not an MBS suffix; claim it as 13876. All 13876 criteria apply.
rules: Counts as 1 of the maximum 4 pressure types per calendar day
PAWP is not listed as a separate MBS pressure type – it is measured through the same PA catheter (interpretation)
PA catheter insertion, including wedge pressure and cardiac output measurement, is item 13818

title: 13876 – cardiac intracavity pressure (practice code R)
criteria: Practice shorthand for item 13876 claimed for continuous monitoring of a cardiac intracavity pressure (e.g. right atrial/right ventricular, or a left atrial line) in ICU. 'R' is not an MBS suffix; claim it as 13876. All 13876 criteria apply.
rules: Counts as 1 of the maximum 4 pressure types per calendar day

Caution: right atrial pressure read through the same CVC used for CVP is likely to be treated as the same pressure, so claiming both C and R from one catheter risks a duplicate claim (interpretation – not stated in MBS)
Use only where a genuinely separate intracavity pressure is being continuously monitored

title: Airway + ventilation started outside ICU for ICU care
criteria: Establishing airway access and starting mechanical ventilation outside an ICU (e.g. ED, ward, MET call) so the patient can receive ventilatory support in an ICU. The descriptor does not limit who may perform it.
rules: Not payable when started in the context of an anaesthetic for surgery, even if the patient will be ventilated in ICU afterwards – use the anaesthetic items instead (TN.1.10)
No frequency limit is stated
The in-ICU equivalent is 13881

title: Transfusion of blood or bone marrow already collected
criteria: Transfusion of blood or bone marrow that has already been collected. Per TN.1.7 this includes blood, platelets, white cells, bone marrow or gamma globulin.
rules: Not payable when gamma globulin is given intramuscularly (TN.1.7)
The item page states no frequency limit or co-claiming exclusion
Descriptor last updated 1 Mar 2026

title: Central vein catheterisation (incl. US guidance)
criteria: Insertion of a central venous catheter by a percutaneous or open approach, including ultrasound guidance where clinically appropriate. A PICC qualifies only if its tip sits in a central vein (TN.1.6).
rules: No separate ultrasound item is claimable (TN.1.10)
Not for a service covered by item 13318 (descriptor)
PICC tip must be in a central vein, not a peripheral vein (TN.1.6)
No frequency limit is stated
When a CVC is inserted as part of an anaesthetic, the RVG item 22020 is the listed equivalent (TN.10.1)

title: Intra-arterial cannulation (incl. US guidance)
criteria: Arterial cannulation, including ultrasound guidance where clinically appropriate, for intra-arterial pressure monitoring and/or arterial blood sampling.
rules: No separate ultrasound item is claimable (TN.1.10)
If done outside an ICU (e.g. with an anaesthetic), it is payable on top of 13870/13873 on the same day; endorse the account 'performed outside of an Intensive Care Unit' (TN.1.10)
TN.1.10 does not say whether insertion inside the ICU is payable with 13870/13873 (those items include arterial sampling) – check with askMBS before relying on it

title: Right heart (PA) balloon catheter insertion
criteria: Insertion of a right heart balloon flotation (pulmonary artery) catheter, including pulmonary wedge pressure and cardiac output measurement.
rules: Once per day, unless a second discrete operation is performed that day (TN.1.10)
Ongoing PA pressure monitoring in ICU is billed under 13876 (pulmonary arterial pressure)

title: IABP counterpulsation management – each day
criteria: Daily management of intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation, including associated consultations and full haemodynamic assessment and management on several occasions during the day.
rules: Claimable each day, including the first day (the separate first-day item 13847 was deleted in March 2020)
Balloon insertion is not included – it is item 38609 (TN.1.10)
No co-claiming restriction is stated

title: CVVH/CAVH management in ICU – first day
criteria: Management of continuous arteriovenous or venovenous haemofiltration in an ICU on the first day, by a specialist/consultant physician who is immediately available and exclusively rostered for intensive care.
rules: FORM LABEL NOTE: this item covers management only and does not mention inserting the dialysis catheter. Vascular access would be billed under a separate item (e.g. 13815) – interpretation
The MBS wording is 'haemofiltration'. CVVHD/CVVHDF are commonly billed under this item, but the descriptor does not name them (interpretation)
Requires an exclusively rostered, immediately available ICU specialist (descriptor, TN.1.11)
Once per day per patient (TN.1.9)

title: CVVH/CAVH management in ICU – each subsequent day
criteria: Management of continuous arteriovenous or venovenous haemofiltration in an ICU on each day after the first, by a specialist/consultant physician who is immediately available and exclusively rostered for intensive care.
rules: Each day after the first day of haemofiltration management (descriptor)
Requires an exclusively rostered ICU specialist (TN.1.11)
Once per day per patient (TN.1.9)
Patient must be in an ICU that meets TN.1.9

title: Epidural/intrathecal/CSE infusion – initial injection
criteria: Initial injection or start of an intrathecal, combined spinal-epidural or epidural infusion of a therapeutic substance, including up to 1 hour of continuous attendance by the practitioner.
rules: Group T7 (regional blocks): used for pain or labour not associated with an operation, including labour epidurals. For >1 h of continuous attendance use 18219; after-hours labour equivalents are 18226/18227 (TN.10.7)
Only one attendance: not claimable for a further attendance just to optimise (extend or improve) an existing block (TN.10.7)
If the anaesthetist inserts it with anaesthesia and surgery for post-op pain, use RVG item 22031 instead
Subsequent top-ups/revisions: 18222 (≤15 min attendance) or 18225 (>15 min)

title: Regional catheter – subsequent injection/revision >15 min
criteria: A subsequent injection into, or revision of, a continuous catheter infusion of a therapeutic substance (not contrast) used to maintain regional anaesthesia or analgesia (e.g. an epidural), where the practitioner is in continuous attendance for more than 15 minutes.
rules: FORM LABEL NOTE: not a 'daily maintenance' item – it is billed per subsequent injection/revision with >15 min of continuous attendance; ≤15 min is 18222
Not payable to the operating surgeon in the post-op period, which counts as routine aftercare (TN.7.2)
No daily frequency limit is stated on the item page

title: Specialist initial attendance (referred)
criteria: Initial attendance in a single course of treatment by a specialist practising in their specialty, at consulting rooms or in hospital, after the patient has been referred.
rules: Valid referral required
Not with items 106, 109, 125 or 16401 (descriptor)
An intensivist billing 13870/13873 for the patient that day should not also bill 104 – the ICU fee covers all ICU attendances by the ICU specialist (TN.1.11; interpretation)
A specialist asked to see an ICU patient who is not managing the ICU care may claim; endorse the account as not part of ICU management (TN.1.9)
Several attendances on one day are payable only if each is not a continuation of the last and there is a reasonable gap; record the times (AN.0.7)
Video equivalent is 91822 (AN.40.1)

title: Specialist subsequent attendance (referred)
criteria: Any attendance after the initial one in a single course of treatment by a specialist practising in their specialty, at consulting rooms or in hospital, following referral.
rules: Not with items 126 or 16404 (descriptor)
Not payable for the same practitioner, patient and day as a Group T8 operation with a schedule fee above about $350 (AN.0.70 cites $349.95; AN.3.1 cites $359.05)
Same ICU interaction as 104: not alongside the managing intensivist's own 13870/13873 (interpretation of TN.1.11)
Multiple same-day attendances: AN.0.7 applies (not a continuation, reasonable gap, times recorded)
Telehealth equivalents: video 91823, phone 91833

title: Prolonged attendance – imminent danger of death, 1–2 h
criteria: Attendance by a GP, specialist or consultant physician on a patient in imminent danger of death, totalling at least 1 hour but less than 2 hours, where no other item applies.
rules: FORM LABEL NOTE: this is not an 'initial consult' item – it needs a patient in imminent danger of death and at least 60 min of total attendance
Attendance need not be continuous; the total time counts (AN.0.27)
Each practitioner attending at the same time may claim (AN.0.27)
Only where no other item applies (descriptor), so likely not for ICU patients whose care that day is billed by the same intensivist under 13870/13873 (interpretation)

title: Goals of care outside ICU by intensivist (≥60 min)
criteria: At least 60 minutes spent preparing goals of care, outside an ICU, for a gravely ill patient who has no current goals of care, by an intensive care specialist who takes overall responsibility for preparing them. It requires a comprehensive evaluation, a capacity assessment, discussion with the patient or surrogate (offering alternatives to intensive or escalated care), and agreed goals recorded where other clinicians can readily find them.
rules: FORM LABEL NOTE: not a general ward consult – it is specifically a ≥60-min goals-of-care service

Gravely ill = life-threatening acute illness/injury, or acute illness plus high risk of death within 12 months; more than one management option is clinically appropriate; and there is no retrievable goals-of-care record, or the existing one is expected to change substantially (TN.1.11)

Once per admission, counting ED goals-of-care items 5039/5041/5042/5044. Can be claimed again only if a later ICU referral or MET/cardiac arrest call substantively changes the clinical situation (TN.1.11)
Not with 13870 or 13873 on the same day (TN.1.11)
Not claimable if the goals of care cover only some of the patient's major issues (TN.1.11)
Record on standard facility forms where available; provider should be trained in end-of-life/goals-of-care discussions (TN.1.11)

title: Cardioversion (not during cardiac surgery)
criteria: Restoring cardiac rhythm by electrical stimulation (cardioversion), other than during cardiac surgery.
rules: The item page has no explanatory notes or co-claiming restrictions
Carries an anaesthetic value: anaesthesia by a different practitioner is item 20410

title: Intercostal drain insertion (no rib resection)
criteria: Insertion of an intercostal drain, not involving rib resection and excluding aftercare.
rules: Not with items 38815, 38816 or 38829–38834 (descriptor); 38829 is an intercostal drain with pleurodesis
FORM LABEL NOTE: pleurocentesis is NOT this item – diagnostic aspiration is 38800 and therapeutic drainage is 38803
Group T8 multiple operation rule applies: 100% / 50% / 25% for the 1st / 2nd / 3rd and later operations on one occasion (TN.8.2)
Aftercare is excluded

title: Lumbar puncture
criteria: Lumbar puncture.
rules: Group T8 multiple operation rule applies (TN.8.2)
No other item-specific rules on the page; has an anaesthetic value

title: Tracheostomy – percutaneous technique
criteria: Tracheostomy performed by a percutaneous technique.
rules: Percutaneous technique only; open tracheostomy is a different item (not verified here)
Group T8 multiple operation rule applies (TN.8.2)

Anaesthesia for the tracheostomy (20320) must be given by a different practitioner – anaesthesia items are not payable to the practitioner doing the procedure, except in special circumstances (TN.10.7)

title: Bronchoscopy as an independent procedure
criteria: Bronchoscopy performed as an independent procedure.
rules: 'Independent procedure' – i.e. not done as part of another operation (interpretation)
Group T8 multiple operation rule applies (TN.8.2)
No ICU-specific notes or exclusions on the page

title: Intracranial pressure monitoring – each day
criteria: Monitoring of intracranial pressure through an intraventricular or subdural catheter, subarachnoid bolt or similar, by a specialist or consultant physician, each day.
rules: Daily item
No explanatory notes or exclusions on the item page
Covers monitoring only; the descriptor does not include inserting the device

title: Arterial puncture for diagnostic blood sample
criteria: Arterial puncture and collection of blood for diagnostic purposes.
rules: Not payable in addition to 13870 or 13873 on the same day (TN.1.10)

title: Ventricular assist device management – first day
criteria: Management of a ventricular assist device on the first day, for a patient admitted to an ICU for implantation of the device or for complications of its implantation or management.
rules: Excludes an intravascular microaxial VAD inserted into the right ventricle (descriptor)
The ICU admission must be for implantation or for device complications
Once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved (TN.1.10)
Later days are 13854

title: Ventricular assist device management – each later day
criteria: Management of a ventricular assist device for a patient in an ICU, including complications of implantation or management, on each day after the first.
rules: Excludes an intravascular microaxial VAD inserted into the right ventricle (descriptor)
Once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved (TN.1.10)

title: Temporary transvenous pacing electrode insertion
criteria: Insertion of a temporary transvenous pacemaking electrode.
rules: Group T8 multiple operation rule applies (TN.8.2)
No imaging requirement or exclusions on the item page

title: Pre-anaesthesia consultation – brief (≤15 min)
criteria: A brief pre-anaesthesia consultation (15 minutes or less) by an anaesthetist: targeted history, limited examination including the cardiorespiratory system, and a brief discussion of the anaesthesia plan.
rules: Payable even if the procedure does not go ahead (TN.6.1)
Included in the anaesthetic unless it is a separate attendance away from the operating theatre/induction room (TN.10.7)
Not with pain specialist items 2801–3000 (descriptor, TN.6.1)
Only active time with the patient counts, not discussion with colleagues (TN.6.1)
Longer/complex consults: 17615 (15–30 min), 17620 (30–45 min), 17625 (>45 min). These need advanced surgery or complex medical problems plus a written anaesthesia plan (TN.6.1)

title: Anaes: complex upper GI endoscopy (bleed/ERCP/EUS/PEG/EMR)
criteria: Anaesthesia for upper GI endoscopy for acute GI haemorrhage, ERCP, upper GI endoscopic ultrasound, PEG, or endoscopic mucosal resection of a tumour. 7 basic units.
rules: FORM LABEL NOTE: anaesthesia for routine upper GI endoscopy is 20740 (5 units); 20745 is only for the listed complex procedures
Payable only with an eligible service, i.e. a procedure carrying an anaesthetic value (TN.10.2)
Fee = basic units + time units (23010–24136) + any modifiers (25000–25050); $23.70 per unit in the 2026 schedule
Not payable to the practitioner who performs the procedure, except in special circumstances (TN.10.7)
Anaesthesia start and end times must be recorded in writing (TN.10.3)

title: Anaes: neck procedures (incl. larynx/trachea)
criteria: Anaesthesia for procedures on the oesophagus, thyroid, larynx, trachea, lymphatic system, muscles, nerves or other deep tissues of the neck, where no other item in the subgroup applies. 6 basic units.
rules: No tracheostomy-specific RVG item was found; tracheostomy falls under 'trachea' here
Eligible service required (TN.10.2); fee = basic + time + modifiers
Not payable to the practitioner doing the tracheostomy (TN.10.7)
Start and end times must be recorded (TN.10.3)

title: Anaes: closed chest procedures (incl. bronchoscopy)
criteria: Anaesthesia for all closed chest procedures, including rigid oesophagoscopy or bronchoscopy, where no other item in the intrathoracic subgroup applies. 6 basic units.
rules: Eligible service required (TN.10.2); fee = basic + time + modifiers
Not payable to the practitioner doing the bronchoscopy (TN.10.7)
Start and end times must be recorded (TN.10.3)

title: Anaes: transoesophageal echocardiography
criteria: Anaesthesia for a 2-dimensional real-time transoesophageal examination of the heart. 5 basic units.
rules: Eligible service required (TN.10.2); fee = basic + time + modifiers
Not payable to the practitioner doing the TOE (TN.10.7)
Start and end times must be recorded (TN.10.3)

title: Anaes: electrical cardioversion
criteria: Anaesthesia for electrical conversion of arrhythmias (cardioversion). 4 basic units.
rules: Eligible service required, e.g. 13400 (TN.10.2); fee = basic + time + modifiers
Not payable to the practitioner who performs the cardioversion (TN.10.7)
Start and end times must be recorded (TN.10.3)

title: Anaes: CT / MRI / digital subtraction angiography
criteria: Anaesthesia for CT scanning, MRI scanning or digital subtraction angiography. 6 basic units.
rules: Descriptor lists CT, MRI and DSA only; other angiographic/interventional procedures may fall under other subgroup 17 items (not checked)
Eligible service required (TN.10.2); fee = basic + time + modifiers
Start and end times must be recorded (TN.10.3)

title: Anaesthesia modifier – patient aged 75+
criteria: Modifier added to anaesthesia, perfusion or assistance at anaesthesia when the patient is 75 years or older. 1 unit.
rules: Not a stand-alone item; claim only with anaesthesia, assistance at anaesthesia or perfusion (22060) (TN.10.3)
The modifier for patients under 4 years is 25013

title: Anaesthesia modifier – emergency (immediate treatment)
criteria: Modifier for anaesthesia, perfusion or assistance at anaesthesia where the patient needs immediate treatment, without which there would be a significant threat to life or a body part. 2 units.
rules: Not with 25025, 25030 or 25050 (descriptor); emergency and after-hours emergency modifiers cannot both be claimed (TN.10.3)
Use 25020 (not 25025) if 50% or less of the emergency service time falls after hours (TN.10.3)
Not a stand-alone item (TN.10.3)

title: Anaesthesia modifier – after-hours emergency
criteria: Modifier for emergency anaesthesia (immediate treatment needed to avoid a significant threat to life or a body part) where more than 50% of the service time falls between 8 pm and 8 am on a weekday, or at any time on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday.
rules: No fixed fee: it adds 50% of the anaesthesia fee, i.e. basic units + time units + any applicable 25000–25014 modifiers + associated 22002–22051 services (descriptor)
More than 50% of the service time must fall in the after-hours period, otherwise use 25020 (TN.10.3)
Must also meet the emergency definition
Not with 25020 (TN.10.3); the assistant's equivalent is 25030

title: Anaesthesia time: 16–30 min (2 units)
criteria: Anaesthesia time unit item for a total anaesthesia time of 16 to 30 minutes. 2 units.
rules: Time starts when the anaesthetist begins exclusive, continuous care of the patient and ends at safe handover to other staff (TN.10.3)
Up to 2 h: 1 unit per 15 min or part thereof; beyond 2 h: 1 unit per 10 min or part thereof (TN.10.3)
Start and end times must be recorded in writing or the item does not apply (TN.10.3)
Claim the one time item that matches the total time (interpretation of the banded structure); ≤15 min is 23010

title: Anaesthesia time: 31–45 min (3 units)
criteria: Anaesthesia time unit item for a total anaesthesia time of 31 to 45 minutes. 3 units.
rules: Same time-counting and recording rules as 23025 (TN.10.3)

title: Anaesthesia time: 46–60 min (4 units)
criteria: Anaesthesia time unit item for a total anaesthesia time of 46 minutes to 1 hour. 4 units.
rules: Same time-counting and recording rules as 23025 (TN.10.3)

title: Anaesthesia time: 1:01–1:15 h (5 units)
criteria: Anaesthesia time unit item for a total anaesthesia time of 1 h 01 min to 1 h 15 min. 5 units.
rules: Same time-counting and recording rules as 23025 (TN.10.3)

title: Anaesthesia time: 1:16–1:30 h (6 units)
criteria: Anaesthesia time unit item for a total anaesthesia time of 1 h 16 min to 1 h 30 min. 6 units.
rules: Same time-counting and recording rules as 23025 (TN.10.3)
Longer anaesthetics use the higher time items up to 24136

title: ASA 3 modifier – severe systemic disease
criteria: Modifier for anaesthesia, perfusion or assistance at anaesthesia where the patient has severe systemic disease (ASA physical status 3). 1 unit.
rules: ASA 3 = severe systemic disease that significantly limits activity, e.g. severely limiting heart disease, diabetes with vascular complications, dialysis-dependent renal failure (TN.10.3)
No modifier for ASA 1–2 (TN.10.3)
Not a stand-alone item (TN.10.3)

title: ASA 4 modifier – constant threat to life
criteria: Modifier for anaesthesia, perfusion or assistance at anaesthesia where the patient has severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life (ASA physical status 4). 2 units.
rules: Examples: angina at rest/minimal exertion, end-stage emphysema (TN.10.3)
Not a stand-alone item (TN.10.3)

title: ASA 5 modifier – moribund
criteria: Modifier for anaesthesia, perfusion or assistance at anaesthesia where the patient is not expected to survive 24 hours with or without the operation (ASA physical status 5). 3 units.
rules: Examples: ruptured AAA with profound shock, major head injury with rising ICP, massive PE (TN.10.3)
Not a stand-alone item (TN.10.3)

title: ECMO: peripheral cannulation for VA ECLS
criteria: Peripheral cannulation for veno-arterial cardiopulmonary extracorporeal life support (VA ECMO), including ultrasound guidance where clinically appropriate. NOT ON FORM – answers the ECMO question.
rules: No separate ultrasound item claimable (TN.1.10)
ECLS items are payable once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved (TN.1.10)
The descriptor does not restrict who may perform it

title: ECMO: VA ECLS management – first day
criteria: Management of veno-arterial cardiopulmonary extracorporeal life support on the first day. Yes – this is the MBS item for VA ECMO management (introduced 1 Mar 2020). NOT ON FORM.
rules: Once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved, so only one practitioner can claim per day (TN.1.10)
Covers ECLS services provided in an ICU (TN.1.10)
The notes do not say whether it can be claimed alongside 13870/13873 (not addressed)
Later days are 13835

title: ECMO: VA ECLS management – each later day
criteria: Management of veno-arterial cardiopulmonary extracorporeal life support on each day after the first. NOT ON FORM.
rules: Once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved (TN.1.10)
ICU setting (TN.1.10)

title: ECMO: VV ECLS management – first day
criteria: Management of veno-venous pulmonary extracorporeal life support (VV ECMO) on the first day. NOT ON FORM.
rules: Once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved (TN.1.10)
ICU setting (TN.1.10)
Later days are 13838

title: ECMO: VV ECLS management – each later day
criteria: Management of veno-venous pulmonary extracorporeal life support on each day after the first. NOT ON FORM.
rules: Once per calendar day per patient, however many practitioners are involved (TN.1.10)
ICU setting (TN.1.10)

title: ECMO: peripheral cannulation for VV ECLS
criteria: Peripheral cannulation for veno-venous pulmonary extracorporeal life support, including ultrasound guidance where clinically appropriate. NOT ON FORM.
rules: No separate ultrasound item claimable (TN.1.10)
Once per calendar day per patient (TN.1.10)

title: Anaes: upper GI endoscopic procedures (routine)
criteria: Anaesthesia for upper gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures. 5 basic units. NOT ON FORM – probably the correct item for routine gastroscopy, rather than 20745.
rules: Eligible service required (TN.10.2); fee = basic + time + modifiers
Not payable to the endoscopist (TN.10.7)

title: Pleural aspiration – diagnostic
criteria: Aspiration of the thoracic cavity for diagnostic purposes. NOT ON FORM – diagnostic pleurocentesis.
rules: Not with 38803 (descriptor)

title: Pleural aspiration – therapeutic drainage
criteria: Aspiration of the thoracic cavity with therapeutic drainage (paracentesis), with or without a diagnostic sample. NOT ON FORM – therapeutic pleurocentesis.
rules: Use instead of 38800 when therapeutic drainage is done

title: Regional catheter – subsequent injection/revision ≤15 min
criteria: A subsequent injection into, or revision of, a continuous catheter infusion used to maintain regional anaesthesia or analgesia, where continuous attendance is 15 minutes or less. NOT ON FORM – the short-attendance counterpart of 18225.
rules: Not payable to the operating surgeon in the post-op period (TN.7.2)
Labour epidural top-ups use 18222/18225 (TN.10.7)

title: Epidural/intrathecal for post-op pain with anaesthesia
criteria: Initial intrathecal or epidural injection of a therapeutic substance (with or without a catheter) in association with anaesthesia and surgery, for post-operative pain management. 5 basic units. NOT ON FORM – used instead of 18216 when the epidural is part of an anaesthetic.
rules: Not with item 22036 (descriptor)
Only in association with anaesthesia and surgery
